split_reasoning: One activity, designing tests; plans, scenarios, scripts and procedures are alternative forms of the same test-design deliverable.

parts.text: Design the test plan and test cases (scenarios, scripts, procedures) for a feature or release.
parts.type_reasoning: Each design effort produces a test plan or set of test cases that the team reviews and then executes.
parts.unit_reasoning: Test design is handed over per feature or release as a test plan or test-case set that goes into review in the test management tool.
parts.work_item: one test plan or test-case set for a feature or release
parts.start: requirements or user stories for the feature/release received
parts.end: test plan and cases written, reviewed and baselined in the test management tool
parts.checked_by: QA lead / test manager, and developers or product owner who review coverage

notes: Overlaps heavily with 14640 (testing programs by area) and 14648 (documenting procedures); boundaries between these three statements are blurry.

split_reasoning: One activity: testing a system change before it is released.

parts.text: Test a system modification in the test environment and report whether it is ready for implementation.
parts.type_reasoning: Each modification tested ends in test results and a go/no-go recommendation that release decisions rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Changes arrive for testing as individual change requests or builds, and each gets a test sign-off.
parts.work_item: one system modification (change request or build) tested and signed off
parts.start: modification deployed to the test environment and assigned for testing
parts.end: test cases executed, results recorded and pass/fail sign-off given for implementation
parts.checked_by: release manager / change board and development lead

split_reasoning: One activity, building test suites; the listed areas (database impacts, regression, negative testing, retests, usability) are different coverage areas of the same deliverable.

parts.text: Develop a test suite covering a given testing area (e.g. regression, negative, database-impact or usability tests) for an application.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a test suite that is reviewed and then used in test cycles.
parts.unit_reasoning: Testing programs are built and handed over as a suite for one area of one application, not test by test.
parts.work_item: one test suite for one testing area of an application
parts.start: decision to cover a testing area (e.g. need for a regression suite) and review of the application scope
parts.end: suite of test cases written, reviewed and added to the test repository

notes: Essentially the same work as 14638 at a slightly different grain.

split_reasoning: Documenting a defect in the tracker and reporting it to developers is one step: the filed bug report is the report.

parts.text: Write up a software defect in the bug tracking system and assign or report it to the developers.
parts.type_reasoning: Each defect produces a bug report that developers rely on to reproduce and fix the problem.
parts.unit_reasoning: The bug ticket is the unit that enters the developers' queue.
parts.work_item: one bug report filed
parts.start: defect observed during testing
parts.end: ticket filed with steps to reproduce, severity and evidence, and assigned to developers
parts.checked_by: developer who picks up the bug and QA lead during triage

split_reasoning: Identifying, analyzing and documenting a problem are consecutive steps toward one deliverable, a documented problem; the listed problem areas are just kinds of problem.

parts.text: Identify and analyze a problem with program function, output, screen or content, and document it.
parts.type_reasoning: Each problem found ends in a written-up problem that others act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Problems are handed over one at a time as documented issues.
parts.work_item: one program problem analyzed and documented
parts.start: unexpected behavior, output or content noticed
parts.end: problem isolated, reproduced and written up with analysis
parts.checked_by: developer who fixes it and QA lead

notes: Nearly the same work item as 14641; 14642 puts more weight on the analysis before the write-up.

split_reasoning: Monitoring bug resolution is ongoing and yields two kinds of item: following individual defects through to closure, and reporting on resolution progress.

parts.text: Follow up an open defect, verify the fix when delivered and update or close the ticket.
parts.type_reasoning: Each defect followed up ends in a ticket status change (closed, reopened) that the team relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Defect tickets are the unit tracked and closed in the bug tracker.
parts.work_item: one defect followed through to verified closure or reopening
parts.start: defect marked fixed or overdue in the tracker
parts.end: fix retested and ticket closed, or reopened with notes

parts.text: Prepare a periodic defect-status report tracking resolution progress and success rates.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a report that managers read to track quality and release progress.
parts.unit_reasoning: The status report is what is sent, usually per sprint, week or release.
parts.work_item: one defect-status / resolution report (weekly, per sprint or per release)
parts.start: pull of defect data from the tracker for the period
parts.end: report with open/closed counts, trends and blockers sent to stakeholders

notes: Fix retesting in part a also appears in 14640 ('error or bug retests'). Time shares are a judgment.

split_reasoning: Creating a defect database is a rare setup job, while maintaining it is continuing curation; these are different kinds of work.

parts.text: Set up a database or tracker project for known test defects.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a configured database that the team then uses.
parts.unit_reasoning: A new defect database or project is set up and handed to the team as one piece.
parts.work_item: one known-defect database or tracker project set up
parts.start: need for a defect repository for a product or project identified
parts.end: database configured with fields, workflow and access, and released to the team
parts.checked_by: QA lead and team members who use it

parts.text: Review and clean up records in the known-defect database (update statuses, merge duplicates, add known-issue notes).
parts.type_reasoning: Maintenance is ongoing, but it is done in batches that leave the database in a checked state others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Maintenance is usually done as a periodic pass or triage session over a set of records, not record by record.
parts.work_item: one maintenance pass over a batch of known-defect records
parts.start: scheduled review or triage of the defect list
parts.end: records updated, duplicates merged and known-issues list current
parts.checked_by: QA lead, developers and support staff who rely on the known-issues list

notes: Many teams use a commercial bug tracker, so 'create' may mostly be configuration; the 0.2/0.8 split is a judgment.

split_reasoning: Planning schedules and strategies is one planning activity producing one test plan document for a project.

parts.text: Plan the test strategy and schedule for a project or release to fit its scope and delivery dates.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a test strategy or schedule that managers approve and the team follows.
parts.unit_reasoning: A test strategy/schedule is written and approved per project or release.
parts.work_item: one test strategy and schedule for a project or release
parts.start: project scope and delivery dates received
parts.end: test strategy and schedule approved by project and QA management

notes: Could be folded into the test plan of 14638 in some organizations.

split_reasoning: One activity: taking part in design review meetings; the listed topics are just what the input covers.

parts.text: Take part in product design reviews, giving input on requirements, designs, schedules and potential problems.
parts.type_reasoning: The value is in contributing during the review meeting; usually nothing separately checkable is produced by the tester.

notes: Some reviews are done asynchronously with written comments on a design document, which would make that portion DISCRETE.

split_reasoning: One activity, reviewing a document; accuracy, compliance, completeness and risk are criteria of the same review.

parts.text: Review a software document for technical accuracy, compliance, completeness and risk, and return comments.
parts.type_reasoning: Each review produces comments or a sign-off that the document's author relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Documents are reviewed and signed off one at a time.
parts.work_item: one software document reviewed with comments returned
parts.start: document (spec, user guide, release notes) submitted for review
parts.end: review comments or approval returned to the author
parts.checked_by: document author and document owner / QA lead

split_reasoning: One activity: writing up test procedures.

parts.text: Document a test procedure so that it can be repeated and meets standards.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a procedure document that other testers and auditors rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Procedures are written and approved one document at a time.
parts.work_item: one test procedure document written or updated
parts.start: test procedure designed or changed
parts.end: procedure document reviewed and stored in the test repository
parts.checked_by: QA lead and compliance / audit reviewers

notes: Overlaps with 14638, which also mentions procedures.

split_reasoning: One activity: defining quality standards or release criteria; standards, methods and procedures are forms of the same deliverable.

parts.text: Write a standard, method or procedure that defines product quality or release-readiness criteria.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a standard that management approves and teams follow.
parts.unit_reasoning: Standards are drafted and approved as individual documents.
parts.work_item: one quality standard or release-readiness criteria document
parts.start: need for a new or revised quality standard identified
parts.end: standard approved and published to teams
parts.checked_by: QA manager and engineering / release management

split_reasoning: One activity: updating automated test scripts after application changes.

parts.text: Update automated test scripts to match a change in the application.
parts.type_reasoning: Each update produces revised scripts that are code-reviewed and run in the pipeline.
parts.unit_reasoning: Script updates are handed over as a code change (pull request) per application change or failing set of scripts.
parts.work_item: one set of automated test scripts updated (one pull request)
parts.start: application change or failing/outdated scripts identified
parts.end: updated scripts pass review and run green in the test pipeline

split_reasoning: One activity: investigating an escalated customer problem.

parts.text: Investigate a customer problem escalated by technical support.
parts.type_reasoning: Each escalation ends in findings returned to support or a bug filed.
parts.unit_reasoning: Escalations arrive as individual tickets from the support queue.
parts.work_item: one escalated customer problem investigated
parts.start: escalation ticket received from technical support
parts.end: problem reproduced or ruled out, findings returned to support and bug filed if needed
parts.checked_by: technical support staff and development team

split_reasoning: Installing and maintaining testing tools is different work from using them to run tests, so split; install and maintain are one kind of tool-administration work.

parts.text: Install, upgrade or configure a software testing tool.
parts.type_reasoning: Each installation or upgrade leaves a working tool the team relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Tool installs and upgrades are done and handed over one at a time, often as a ticket.
parts.work_item: one testing tool installed, upgraded or reconfigured
parts.start: request or need to install or update a testing tool
parts.end: tool working in the test environment and available to the team
parts.checked_by: QA team members who use the tool

parts.text: Use software testing tools to run a test cycle and record results.
parts.type_reasoning: Running tests with the tools produces a set of recorded results others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Test execution is handed over per test run or cycle, with results logged.
parts.work_item: one test run executed with results recorded
parts.start: build ready and test run scheduled
parts.end: tests executed and results logged in the test management tool

notes: 'Use' testing programs is largely the means for test execution covered by other statements (e.g. 14639, 14655).

split_reasoning: Feedback and recommendations on usability and functionality are one deliverable, a set of comments for developers.

parts.text: Give developers written feedback and recommendations on a feature's usability and functionality.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces feedback that developers read and act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Feedback is usually given per feature or build, as a ticket, comment set or short write-up.
parts.work_item: one set of usability/functionality recommendations for a feature or build
parts.start: feature or build available for evaluation
parts.end: recommendations sent to developers or logged as improvement tickets

notes: Some of this feedback is given verbally in stand-ups or reviews, which would be INTERPERSONAL.

split_reasoning: Monitoring performance is ongoing and yields two kinds of item: investigating specific performance problems, and periodic performance reporting.

parts.text: Investigate a performance problem or anomaly seen in monitoring or test results.
parts.type_reasoning: Each anomaly ends in a finding and usually a ticket that others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Performance anomalies are handled one at a time and closed or turned into bug tickets.
parts.work_item: one performance anomaly investigated
parts.start: alert, slow response or degraded metric observed
parts.end: cause recorded and bug filed or anomaly closed as no action

parts.text: Prepare a periodic program performance report.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a report that managers and developers read.
parts.unit_reasoning: The report is what is sent per period or per release.
parts.work_item: one performance report (per period or release)
parts.start: pull of performance metrics for the period or build
parts.end: report with trends and issues sent to stakeholders

split_reasoning: One activity: compatibility testing; programs, hardware, operating systems and networks are alternative environments for the same test cycle.

parts.text: Run compatibility tests of a build across a set of programs, hardware, operating systems or network environments.
parts.type_reasoning: Each test cycle produces a compatibility results matrix that release decisions rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Compatibility testing is done and reported per build across a configuration matrix.
parts.work_item: one compatibility test cycle for a build across a configuration matrix
parts.start: build and list of target configurations received
parts.end: results matrix recorded and incompatibilities filed as bugs

notes: Testing on physical hardware or devices may involve some hands-on setup away from the computer; not split out because it is usually a small share.

split_reasoning: One activity: building a production-like test environment; installing and configuring are steps of the same deliverable.

parts.text: Install and configure a replica of the production environment for performance testing.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a working test environment that testers rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Environments are built and handed over one at a time, usually against a request.
parts.work_item: one production-like test environment built and configured
parts.start: request for a test environment matching production
parts.end: environment configured, verified against production settings and handed to testers
parts.checked_by: testers using it and QA / operations lead

notes: If physical servers must be racked or cabled, part of this work would be PHYSICAL; today it is mostly virtual.

split_reasoning: One activity: diagnosing a problem together with field staff or a customer and recommending a fix.

parts.text: Work with field staff or a customer to diagnose a problem and recommend a solution.
parts.type_reasoning: The work happens in live conversations with field staff or customers and ends in a recommended solution recorded on the case.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each field or customer problem is handled as one case, which ends with a recommendation.
parts.work_item: one field/customer problem case diagnosed with a recommended solution
parts.start: field staff or customer raises a problem needing QA input
parts.end: diagnosis and recommended solution given and recorded on the case
parts.checked_by: field staff or customer, and technical support

notes: Could be read as DISCRETE if most diagnosis is done offline; overlaps with 14651.

split_reasoning: Identifying deviations and suggesting fixes are two steps of one standards review.

parts.text: Review a program against standards and suggest modifications to bring it into compliance.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a list of deviations and suggested changes that developers act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Compliance reviews are done per program, module or release and handed over as findings.
parts.work_item: one program or module reviewed for standards compliance with suggested modifications
parts.start: program or module submitted for standards review
parts.end: deviations and suggested modifications sent to developers

split_reasoning: One activity: building automated testing tools; design and development are steps of the same deliverable.

parts.text: Design and develop an automated testing tool or framework component.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a tool that is code-reviewed and used by the test team.
parts.unit_reasoning: Tool work is handed over per tool or feature, as a reviewed code change or release.
parts.work_item: one automated testing tool or framework feature delivered
parts.start: need for a test tool or framework feature defined
parts.end: tool or feature reviewed, merged and available to testers
parts.checked_by: automation lead / peer reviewers and testers using it

notes: A whole framework could be project-scale; the item is meant as one tool or feature.

split_reasoning: Coordinating outside testing mixes setting up and closing out a test round, which produces documents, with live liaison with the testers.

parts.text: Organize a round of user or third-party testing: prepare scope, schedule and tester instructions, and consolidate the results.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a test-round plan and a consolidated results summary that managers rely on for sign-off.
parts.unit_reasoning: User acceptance or third-party testing is organized and signed off per test round.
parts.work_item: one user/third-party test round organized, with consolidated results
parts.start: decision to run user or third-party testing for a release
parts.end: results consolidated and summary or sign-off sent to project management

parts.text: Liaise with users or third-party testers during testing, answering questions and keeping them on track.
parts.type_reasoning: The value is in the live coordination; nothing a colleague would check is produced.

notes: A test round may be close to project scale; time shares are a judgment.

split_reasoning: One activity: initial debugging; configuration files, logs and code are alternative inputs.

parts.text: Do initial debugging on a failure by reviewing configuration files, logs or code to locate its likely source.
parts.type_reasoning: Each failure debugged ends in a likely cause recorded on the ticket that developers rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Initial debugging is done per failure or ticket and recorded as triage notes.
parts.work_item: one failure triaged to a likely source
parts.start: failure observed or ticket assigned
parts.end: likely source identified and recorded on the ticket for developers

split_reasoning: A beta site visit involves on-site evaluation away from the desk and a separate written report, so split.

parts.text: Travel to a beta testing site and observe and evaluate the software's performance on site.
parts.type_reasoning: Requires being physically present at the customer site.

parts.text: Write up the findings of a beta site visit.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces a visit report that developers and managers rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: One report is written and sent per site visit.
parts.work_item: one beta site visit report
parts.start: return from the site visit with notes and data
parts.end: report with findings and issues sent to development and product management

notes: The on-site part is largely observation and conversation with site staff; it could also be read as INTERPERSONAL.

split_reasoning: Evaluating and recommending are two steps of one tool evaluation.

parts.text: Evaluate candidate testing or bug-tracking software and recommend one.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces an evaluation and recommendation that managers decide on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Tool evaluations are done and handed over one at a time as a recommendation.
parts.work_item: one tool evaluation with recommendation
parts.start: need for a new or replacement testing/bug-tracking tool raised
parts.end: evaluation and recommendation sent to QA or IT management

split_reasoning: One activity: analyzing past test results.

parts.text: Analyze historical test results to find trends and patterns, and report them.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces an analysis that managers and the team use to improve testing.
parts.unit_reasoning: Historical analyses are done and sent as a report, typically per release or period.
parts.work_item: one historical test-results analysis report
parts.start: pull of past test results for the releases or period in scope
parts.end: analysis with trends and recommendations sent to QA management
